STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: The buffering, ETag digest, 304 logic, weak matching, non-200 passthrough, 103 forwarding, Compress stacking, GetHead/Logger/Recoverer, ServeContent and the early-Flush rule all held under probes. The Hijack path differs from the baseline in two ways that are not on the approved list. Probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start (README.md modified, etag.go and etag_test.go added).

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files middleware/zz_probe_test.go, zz_probe2_test.go and zz_probe3_test.go were created and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Writes after a successful Hijack are silently accepted. The baseline returns an error, and the middleware does not. Reproduced over a real httptest.Server with `ResponseController.Hijack` then `w.Write("after")`: baseline `err=http: connection has been hijacked`, with ETag `err=<nil>`. The middleware drops the bytes into the buffer and reports success, so the handler is misled. Cause: `etagWriter.Write` ignores `ew.hijacked`. Fix: return `http.ErrHijacked` from Write, ReadFrom and WriteHeader once hijacked.
- [blocking] Bytes the handler wrote before Hijack change the wire output. Baseline sends the status line and headers before the raw bytes (`HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... Transfer-Encoding: chunked ... RAW`). With ETag the client gets only `RAW`, with no status line. The approved list covers only Flush, so this is an unapproved difference. Fix: when hijacking a buffered 200, flush the held status and headers to the underlying writer first, or refuse with the same behaviour as net/http.
- [minor] Content-Type sniffing can differ if the handler calls Flush between small writes (the Flush is a no-op, so sniffing runs on the whole body). Not reproduced in a probe; a suspicion only.

CHECKS:
- Multi-write, io.Copy/ReadFrom, and OneByteReader bodies vs one Write → same ETag, `sha256("hello world")` digest correct → pass
- Empty GET → ETag of empty body; empty HEAD → no ETag → pass
- HEAD with GET-style body over a real server (`http.Head`, GetHead, Logger, Recoverer outside) → same ETag as GET, empty body, If-None-Match gives 304 → pass
- If-None-Match matrix (weak, lists, empties, whitespace, `"ab"` vs `"abc"`, `"ABC"`, malformed, `*`, multiple lines, `W/` on response) → all as spec → pass
- Handler-set invalid ETag `abc` matches only `*` → pass
- 304 header set (Content-Type/Length/Encoding/Last-Modified removed; Cache-Control/Vary/Expires/Content-Location/custom kept) → pass
- Non-200 statuses 201/204/206/301/304/404/500 with double WriteHeader and late WriteHeader(299) → pass; body-before-WriteHeader gives implicit 200 → pass
- 103 with Link header over a real server: 103 forwarded, then 200 with ETag → pass
- Late ETag/header set after first write → not leaked → pass
- Recoverer outside ETag, panic after partial write → 500, partial body not sent → pass
- Compress(5) inside ETag over a real server, `Accept-Encoding: gzip`: gzip decodes to payload, gzip ETag differs from identity, Vary kept, gzip ETag → 304, identity request with gzip tag → 200 → pass
- http.ServeContent inside ETag: Range → 206, If-None-Match → 304, plain → 200 → pass
- Early Flush with a blocked handler: client gets no headers before the handler finishes → pass
- Hijack without Hijacker → exact wording error → pass (existing test; re-confirmed)
- Race detector on all probes: no races after fixing my own probe's race

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should hijacking after a buffered 200 be fixed, or documented as a deliberate difference? The approved list does not cover it.
